files.purpose: Workspace manifest for @telelean/runner, a private ESM package described as the Node-only engine (shadow workspace, sandboxed Lean runs, gate, LLM harness). files.purpose: Validates and safely renders Lean names written into generated source. A declaration name must be dotted, with no control characters, whitespace or guillemets, no empty component, and at most 1024 chars; a module name must consist of plain identifiers. formatDeclName wraps non-plain components, and every single-component name, in «» so names can never inject commands; modulePath maps A.B.C to A/B/C.lean.

files.purpose: The one wrapper for every Lean-family process: `systemd-run --user --scope` (MemoryMax, MemorySwapMax=0, OOMPolicy=stop), then `setpriv --pdeathsig KILL`, then a SIGTERM-surviving sh keeper, then bwrap with buildBwrapArgs. Defaults are a 4G cap, a 120 s timeout, 32 MiB of captured output per stream and LEAN_NUM_THREADS=4; it checks that the run sits in its own scope's cgroup with an enforced cap and polls cgroup memory every 200 ms. It fails closed (could-not-start) when preflight fails: bwrap, systemd-run, systemctl, setpriv, sh, cgroup v2, the toolchain or the user manager missing (successful preflights are cached). Otherwise it classifies the run as ok, failed, oom, timeout or cancelled from bwrap's --json-status-fd, memory.events and systemd's Result, reports peak memory only from an end-of-run sample, and stops or resets lingering and failed scopes. Runs are cancelled by AbortSignal (registered before the first await) or by cancelRun(runId), which also SIGKILLs every `telelean-<run>-*` unit.

files.purpose:
ClaudeCliBackend runs the user's own `claude` binary headless (`-p`, stream-json input and output, --verbose). Allowed tools are only Read, Glob, Grep, Edit, Write and mcp__telelean__*; Bash, WebFetch, WebSearch, Agent, AskUserQuestion and NotebookEdit are disallowed. It also passes dontAsk permissions, --restricted, an empty --setting-sources, and generated --settings, --strict-mcp-config and system-prompt files.

startSession works in this order:
1. Refuse under the TELELEAN_NO_REAL_CLAUDE tripwire unless the launch is the node test double.
2. Start the MCP tool server and write the config files.
3. Self-test the path guard.
4. Spawn the CLI detached (its own process group).
5. Preflight over the control protocol: initialize must classify the login as a claude.ai subscription, and get_hooks_listing must show the guard.
An init message that reports an API key also stops the session.

ClaudeCliSession streams one turn at a time through an async queue, answers the CLI's control requests with errors, and supports interrupt. close() goes graceful first, then SIGTERM, then SIGKILL on the whole process group; live groups are also SIGTERMed when the host process exits.

files.purpose: FakeBackend/FakeSession is an LlmBackend that replays scripted steps (text, writeFile, edit, read, callTool, usage, rateLimit, sleep, result), so tests, the extension's Test-mode run backend and the walkthrough dry run can exercise everything except the model. File steps are checked in-process with the real path-guard decide() and policy before they touch the shadow. callTool validates arguments with the real zod schemas, calls the session's AgentToolHost, and renders the reply with the MCP server's renderers. Each session emits init on its first turn, a turn nobody has read ends at once as 'interrupted', and later results repeat the last cumulative cost estimate. Fidelity gap: the edit step uses String.prototype.replace, so `$$` or `$&` in newString are treated as replacement patterns, unlike the real Edit tool.

Parses the CLI's stream-json stdout. LineSplitter splits chunks into lines. The stateful StreamNormalizer turns each JSON line into one of two things:

files.purpose: Generates the M1 check file that is fed to `lake env lean --stdin --json`. It imports the fresh modules, sets pp.fullNames true and pp.proofs false, and then runs four probes per declaration, each on its own line: `#check @N`, `#print N`, `#print axioms N` and `#check type_of% @N`. Names that cannot be written safely are recorded as unwritable instead of probed. parseCheckOutput attributes Lean's messages to probes by line and extracts the type, sort, printed keyword and kind, attributes, def value, axioms and sorry use; Lean errors and output it cannot parse are kept as explicit problems, never guessed.

files.purpose:
The pipeline behind refreshLeanFacts:
1. Validate the request and apply the memory guard.
2. Check the toolchain and the project.
3. Hash the sources.
4. Run `lake build <library>` in place under runLean. The given root is the sandbox's shadowDir: the real model root for the M1 workspace, the shadow's build mirror for the M2 gate. .git is masked, and spawnMemoryMax lowers the cap.
5. Parse the Lake log into messages with LSP positions and compute module states.
6. Read each fresh module's .ilean, plus docstrings and source keywords.
7. Run one check file, after a second memory guard.
8. Re-hash the sources to mark stale modules.

Early exits return low-memory, could-not-start, unsupported-toolchain or unsupported-project. A sandbox failure returns its runLean status with only the run facts. Otherwise the status is build-errors, check-errors or ok, with a detail string listing up to five problems.

Doc/code mismatch: it returns 'ok' even when modules went stale or are not-built (outside the root's import closure), whereas core's FactsStatus comment says 'ok' means every module is fresh.
